html:
The Batavian Republic was the state that replaced the Dutch Republic in 1795, after French armies and Dutch "Patriot" revolutionaries drove out the stadtholder William V. It lasted until 1806. Its name came from the Batavi, a Germanic tribe the Dutch saw as their freedom-loving ancestors.

It was a sister republic of revolutionary France and paid for that: a large indemnity, French troops to feed, and war with Britain, which seized Dutch colonies such as the Cape and Ceylon. It nationalised the bankrupt Dutch East India Company in 1796, and the company was dissolved at the end of 1799.

Inside, it changed a great deal. A constitution in 1798 turned a loose union of provinces into one unitary state, with equal rights and the separation of church and state. Coups shifted its course several times. In 1806 Napoleon turned it into the Kingdom of Holland under his brother Louis.
